title: pvVisItClawReader
body:
## pvVisItClawReader

Reads Clawpack/AMRClaw ASCII output through a small .claw boot file whose DIR=, TIME_FILES_SCANF/REGEX and GRID_FILES_SCANF/REGEX (and optional CYCLE_REGEX) lines locate the time-header and grid-data files. The output is a multiblock dataset in which "claw_mesh" holds every grid of every refinement level, with cell-centred solution components. The captured ParaView summary ("a material-ordered format very similar to IOUT=1") does not describe what the plugin source reads. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Write the .claw boot file yourself; pointing FileName at a fort.* data file does not work.
- The VisIt bridge builds this reader only on non-Windows platforms, so it is missing from Windows ParaView installations.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItClawReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItClawReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from Clawpack data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. For Clawpack data these are the solution components (q) of the Clawpack output, cell-centred. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single Clawpack file to read (.claw); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Name the .claw boot file (DIR=, TIME_FILES_SCANF/REGEX, GRID_FILES_SCANF/REGEX lines), not a Clawpack data file. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The Clawpack plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the Clawpack meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The Claw plugin reports one AMR mesh named "claw_mesh"; the bridge places its grids, grouped by level, inside a multiblock child rather than an AMR dataset. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from Clawpack data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The Clawpack plugin declares its variables zone-centred, so this list normally stays empty. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItClawReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
